name: Sulpiride
summary: Sulpiride (Dogmatil) is an antipsychotic used at higher doses for schizophrenia and at low doses for long-lasting low mood and some stomach and dizziness problems; it is used in parts of Europe, Asia, and South America but is not widely available in the US.
description: Sulpiride, sold under brand names including Dogmatil, is an antipsychotic (a substituted benzamide) that blocks specific dopamine receptors (D2 and D3). At higher doses, it is used to treat schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders. At low doses, it can lift mood and help the gut move food along, and it is sometimes prescribed for long-lasting low-grade depression (dysthymia), functional dyspepsia (ongoing indigestion with no clear cause), and vertigo. It is not widely available in the United States but is used in parts of Europe, Asia, and South America.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Sulpiride, marketed under brand names including Dogmatil, is a substituted benzamide antipsychotic with selective dopamine D2 and D3 receptor antagonism. At higher doses, it is used to treat schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders. At low doses, it has antidepressant and prokinetic effects and is sometimes prescribed for dysthymia, functional dyspepsia, and vertigo. It is not widely available in the United States but is used in parts of Europe, Asia, and South America.
